what: *** THE SAME HAND, THE SAME LETTER, INDEXED TWO WAYS ***
the query: act 110 of 1899, San Eugenio - the capital on Anastasia's surname against the capital on Benito's
result: *** THE BEST SINGLE ILLUSTRATION THIS ARCHIVE HAS of why /name/ exists ***
what the index said: FamilySearch read the declarant *** Benito Lerena *** and the mother *** Anastasia Serena *** - two different surnames, from one clerk, on one page, eleven lines apart.
what the act says, or what it means: *** AT 6,000 PIXELS THE TWO CAPITALS ARE THE SAME LETTERFORM, and neither is the S the same hand writes in San Eugenio and San Juan Bautista. *** The mother is *** Anastasia LERENA. *** The pair is not Lerena x Serena at all; it is *** Alvarez x Lerena ***, and the Lerena father the index offered is a grandfather standing at the desk.

what: *** WHAT THE ITALIAN LINE ON THAT ACT COSTS ***
the query: Pedro Lerena, born about 1842, declared ITALIANO on a Uruguayan act of 1910
result: *** IT PUTS THE ITALIAN STOCK INSIDE URUGUAY, UNDER THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN SPELLING ***
what the index said: /name/ keeps an Italian Lerena/Lerina stock apart from this family on purpose, and has always been able to do so by COUNTRY.
what the act says, or what it means: *** THAT SEPARATION NO LONGER HOLDS ON PLACE ALONE. *** Here is a man of the name, Italian-born, farming in the department of San Jose - the same department as the 1846 act this archive rests a couple on - with Uruguayan-born children and grandchildren who are simply LERENA on the record. *** No Uruguayan Lerena can now be assumed to be of this stock because the record is Uruguayan. *** It is not a reason to join the lines; it is a reason to stop treating country as the test.

what: *** THE YEAR FIELD OF THIS COLLECTION CANNOT BE TRUSTED ***
the query: Uruguay, Civil Registration, 1879-2020 (cc=1837849) - two computer-indexed acts read against their plates
result: *** BOTH WERE DATED 1879 BY THE INDEX AND NEITHER IS 1879 ***
what the index said: One is 1899 and sits in a volume labelled *** Artigas. Birth Records 1899-1900. *** The other is 1910 and sits in *** San Jose. Birth Records 1909-1912. *** The index gave both the collection's OPENING YEAR.
what the act says, or what it means: *** SO A DATE-FILTERED SEARCH OF THIS COLLECTION IS MEASURING THE INDEX, NOT THE REGISTER - and 1879 is an artefact bucket that will swallow acts from any year in it. *** Every Uruguayan civil-registration date this archive holds from a machine-indexed entry should be read against the volume label before it is used. Both of these records also say, in FamilySearch's own words, *** This record was indexed by a computer. ***
